notes: AAAI-23 camera-ready version (9 pages incl. references; the supplementary material it refers to is not in the PDF). Text extracted with pymupdf; figures not visible. Drop clause probability p is the swept variable (0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75) within each config group; it is not a tm_config field. Clause counts are as printed ('we use 10,000 clauses'); the paper never says whether they are per class or total (p. 3 only says p=0.75 'is equivalent of dropping 75% of the total clauses per class'), so clauses_scope is not_reported. Implementation is 'custom' (PyCUDA, p. 3). CTM weighting is inferred from 'top k weighted clauses per class' (p. 5). Unlike the arXiv version, no patch size is given (Fig. 2 caption has none). There is no validation set: the best p per dataset is picked from the test results in Tables 1/2 and used as 'TM (DC)' in Tables 3-9, so the best-p rows have selection_on_test=true; other p rows are not_reported. 'averaged over 100 runs' (p. 4) is grammatically attached only to the CIFAR-10/100 sentence, so MNIST/F-MNIST best-p rows have statistic not_reported despite their ± values. MNIST-C (111-112) uses the p chosen on clean MNIST test data; left not_reported. Paper-internal inconsistency: p. 7 says the MR drop for DC TM is 1.45%, but Table 8 gives 78.67-77.12 = 1.55. p. 3 text says 'Table 2 displays the comparison results' for the ML baselines, which are actually Table 3. Not in the record (omission, not an error): NLP inference time 'less than 2.3s per 1000 samples on average on an NVIDIA GTX 1080 GPU' (p. 3). Table 3/4/5/6/7 TM columns duplicate Table 1/2 values.
